headline.title: AI to Learn 2.0: A Deliverable-Oriented Governance Framework and Maturity Rubric for Opaque AI in Learning-Intensive Domains
headline.summary: The article presents a governance framework and maturity rubric aimed at addressing the challenges posed by generative AI in learning-intensive domains. It highlights the issue of proxy failure, where polished AI-generated outputs may not accurately reflect human understanding or skills, and proposes solutions for evaluating AI-assisted work effectively.

articles.title: OpenCLAW-P2P v6.0: Resilient Multi-Layer Persistence, Live Reference Verification, and Production-Scale Evaluation of Decentralized AI Peer Review
articles.summary: The paper introduces OpenCLAW-P2P v6.0, an advanced decentralized platform enabling autonomous AI agents to publish, peer-review, and enhance scientific research without human oversight. Key features include multi-layer persistence, live reference verification, and a production-scale evaluation framework.

articles.title: Forage V2: Knowledge Evolution and Transfer in Autonomous Agent Organizations
articles.summary: Forage V2 enhances the architecture of autonomous agents by expanding from a single expedition to multiple collaborative missions, addressing the issue of denominator blindness in open-world tasks. This version builds on Forage V1's concepts of co-evolving evaluation and method isolation to improve knowledge evolution and transfer within agent organizations.

articles.title: V-tableR1: Process-Supervised Multimodal Table Reasoning with Critic-Guided Policy Optimization
articles.summary: V-tableR1 is a new reinforcement learning framework designed to enhance multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by promoting rigorous and verifiable reasoning through process supervision. This approach addresses the limitations of existing MLLMs that often rely on superficial pattern matching in visual reasoning tasks.

articles.title: AutoGraph-R1: End-to-End Reinforcement Learning for Knowledge Graph Construction
articles.summary: AutoGraph-R1 is a novel framework designed to optimize knowledge graph construction through end-to-end reinforcement learning, addressing the disconnect between KG construction and its application in retrieval-augmented generation systems. This approach aims to enhance the effectiveness of knowledge graphs in improving question answering systems by ensuring that the construction process aligns with downstream application needs.

articles.title: OThink-SRR1: Search, Refine and Reasoning with Reinforced Learning for Large Language Models
articles.summary: The article presents OThink-SRR1, a novel approach that enhances Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for Large Language Models (LLMs) by integrating reinforced learning to improve search, refinement, and reasoning capabilities. This method aims to mitigate challenges associated with irrelevant retrieval noise and high computational costs of processing full documents in dynamic retrieval strategies.

articles.title: Accelerating PayPal's Commerce Agent with Speculative Decoding: An Empirical Study on EAGLE3 with Fine-Tuned Nemotron Models
articles.summary: The article presents an empirical study on the implementation of speculative decoding with EAGLE3 to enhance PayPal's Commerce Agent, utilizing a fine-tuned llama3.1-nemotron-nano-8B-v1 model. The study benchmarks EAGLE3 against NVIDIA NIM on the same hardware, demonstrating improvements in latency and cost through various configurations.

articles.title: Phase 1 Implementation of LLM-generated Discharge Summaries showing high Adoption in a Dutch Academic Hospital
articles.summary: A pilot study at a Dutch academic hospital demonstrated high adoption of an LLM-integrated system for generating discharge summaries, with 379 summaries created by 21 residents and 4 physician assistants over nine weeks. The study highlights the potential of Large Language Models to streamline the time-consuming process of writing medical discharge summaries.

articles.title: LLM Agents Predict Social Media Reactions but Do Not Outperform Text Classifiers: Benchmarking Simulation Accuracy Using 120K+ Personas of 1511 Humans
articles.summary: A recent study benchmarks the accuracy of LLM-powered agents in predicting social media reactions using over 120,000 personas derived from 1,511 humans. The findings indicate that while these agents can replicate aggregate responses, they do not outperform traditional text classifiers in predicting individual reactions.

articles.title: DR-Venus: Towards Frontier Edge-Scale Deep Research Agents with Only 10K Open Data
articles.summary: Researchers have developed DR-Venus, a 4 billion parameter deep research agent designed for edge-scale deployment, utilizing only 10,000 open data sources. The study focuses on enhancing data quality and utilization to effectively train small language models for real-world applications.

articles.title: Cortex 2.0: Grounding World Models in Real-World Industrial Deployment
articles.summary: Cortex 2.0 introduces a new approach to industrial robotic manipulation by grounding world models in real-world deployment, addressing the limitations of existing Vision-Language-Action models that are reactive and struggle with long-horizon tasks. This framework emphasizes proactive decision-making by evaluating potential futures, enhancing reliability across various tasks and object distributions.

articles.title: Mythos and the Unverified Cage: Z3-Based Pre-Deployment Verification for Frontier-Model Sandbox Infrastructure
articles.summary: The article discusses a critical weakness identified in the containment infrastructure for advanced AI models, highlighted by the April 2026 Claude Mythos sandbox escape. It suggests that the escape may be linked to a CWE-190 arithmetic vulnerability in the sandbox's networking code, although this remains unverified.
